subject: POC: private deployment observability — SIEM ingest, log export & tracing hooks
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-fin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bethany Cross <bethany.cross@acme-fin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability POC for private deployment (logs + traces)

Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to validate Redwood running in our VPC/on-prem stack for production — specifically: secure log export to our SIEM, metrics shipping to our internal Prometheus/Grafana, and tracing hooks (Jaeger/OTLP) that tie back to our request/trace IDs.

Top concerns from our compliance and security teams:
- No plaintext egress unless proxied through our outbound proxy (mTLS + customer certs)
- Ability to route logs to Splunk HEC over TLS with token rotation
- Redaction controls for PII in logs and sampled traces
- Audit trail for who pulled telemetry (retention + access logs)

Can you share a concise plan + what you need from our side for a week-long POC (scope, infra prerequisites, sample configs)? Also please include an approximate timeline and any blockers you foresee.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Cloud Ops — Acme Financial Services
(attachment: internal-telemetry-requirements.xlsx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Bethany Cross <bethany.cross@acme-fin.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability POC for private deployment (logs + traces)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely run a focused POC inside your VPC that validates SIEM ingest, Prometheus-compatible metrics export, and OTLP/Jaeger tracing with sampling controls and redaction. High-level plan below; attaching a short scope doc and example forwarder config.

POC scope (5 working days):
1) Day 0–1: Provision a private Redwood Private control plane in your VPC (customer-managed egress). We verify network paths: outbound proxy, mTLS, and firewall rules.
2) Day 2: Deploy the telemetry forwarder (sidecar or daemonset) that ships logs to your Splunk HEC endpoint and metrics to Prometheus pushgateway if needed. We will validate HEC over TLS with token rotation and mutual auth if you require it.
3) Day 3: Enable tracing hooks — OTLP exporter to your Jaeger/OTLP collector. We'll test trace propagation (X-Request-ID correlation) and verify sampled trace capture does not include raw PII values.
4) Day 4: Audit and evidence collection: access logs for telemetry pulls, KMS usage logs for key access, and retention/archival check.
5) Day 5: Wrap-up + handoff: delivery of config snippets, runbook, and a recorded walkthrough.

Prerequisites we need from Acme:
- A secure egress endpoint (proxy URL) and any cert bundles for mTLS (or an allowlist for Redwood forwarder IPs if you prefer).
- Splunk HEC endpoint URL and test token (we recommend a short-lived token for POC).
- Jaeger/OTLP collector endpoint and sample service to exercise traces (we can deploy a small synthetic workload).
- Contact for firewall/security owner to approve quick rule windows.

Technical notes / blockers:
- If your network blocks direct outbound TLS to 3rd-party IPs, we’ll run the forwarder entirely through your proxy — that adds ~1 day for cert/trust validation.
- For strict air-gapped environments we offer an offline artifacts bundle, but that is outside the 5-day scope.
- PII redaction: Redwood can apply regex-based scrubbers on logs and configurable field masking on trace attributes, but we will need a sample of logs/traces to tune rules.

Next steps: if you confirm the POC dates (we can start as early as Mon 2028-04-15), Laura will coordinate infra access and Marcus will own the forwarder config.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security & Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-obsv-poc-scope.pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO C: private deployment observability — SIEM ingest, log export & tracing hooks

Looping to confirm configuration ownership and a rough task split.

Marcus — can you draft the forwarder daemonset (YAML) that supports: HEC over TLS, syslog-tls fallback, HTTP proxy env, and token refresh hooks? Add a small example of field-scrub regexes and an OTLP exporter config. Keep the config param-driven so Acme can toggle sampling and retention.

Mina — I’ll prep the infra runbook and the list of firewall entries we need to request. I’ll also include the minimal Prometheus scrape/export config and a Grafana dashboard template.

I’ll aim to have the first drafts by EOD Thu so we can ship them with the POC kickoff.

—Laura
Senior Product Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Bethany Cross <bethany.cross@acme-fin.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Splunk Partner (eng) <partner-eng@splunk-partner.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability POC for private deployment (logs + traces) — kickoff week confirmed

Jordan —

Thanks, confirmed. We’ll kick off Monday 2028-04-15. Summary of immediate asks from your side to avoid delays:
- Provide a short-lived Splunk HEC token + HEC endpoint (or staging collector).
- Proxy FQDN and any mTLS certs (or firewall allowlist window).
- A sanitized sample of logs/traces (attaching forwarder example to show configurable scrub rules).

Deliverables for POC:
- Working forwarder (daemonset) that ships logs to Splunk HEC over TLS through your proxy.
- OTLP/Jaeger traces exported and correlated to request IDs.
- Documentation: runbook + evidence bundle for audit (KMS access logs, telemetry access logs).
- Optional: quick dashboard with error-rate/latency metrics in Grafana.

If anything changes from your security contacts, please loop them in early — we’ll keep all telemetry within your VPC and use your managed egress.

Best regards,
Mina
